filesize._comment: Three different reasons, kept apart on purpose rather than blurred into one blanket exemption. See _reason_libs, _reason_data and _reason_i18n. An earlier version of this comment claimed every named file was a vendored library; five of them are not, and saying so was worse than the exemption itself.
filesize._reason_binary: The gate counts newline bytes, so a binary registers as hundreds of 'lines' of nothing. addon/BabelChat/img/ holds the addon's icon; app/babelchat_scanner_win.dll is the compiled memory scanner, built from babelchat_scanner_win/ and committed because the Windows build needs it and not every contributor has a Rust toolchain.
filesize._reason_libs: Libs/ is vendored third-party code — LibBabble ships one generated table per locale and is not ours to split. Naming the files individually rather than exempting Libs/ wholesale keeps the cap on any first-party Lua that lands in that tree.
filesize._reason_data: addon/BabelChat/Data/*.lua ARE first-party: they are the inherited Pirson dictionaries, one table per category, in the format the engine indexes. They are data, not logic — splitting Social.lua at line 500 puts half a category in another file for no gain, and the engine already reads them through one map. Exempted knowingly, and only these four; a new file in Data/ is not covered.
filesize._not_exempt: app/phrasebook.py (512) is over the cap and deliberately NOT listed: it is a data table twelve lines over, and splitting it would be worse than leaving it. app/i18n.py and app/overlay.py came off this list once they were actually split — 1263 to 46 and 1221 to 473.
filesize._reason_overlay: app/overlay_gtk.py (1032) is over the cap and still exempt: splitting it is the same job done for the Qt overlay, and it cannot be verified here because gi is not installed on Windows or on CI — a blind refactor of the Linux frontend right before a release is worse than the file being long. Tracked as overlay-split. app/overlay.py came off this list: it is 473 lines now, down from 1221.
filesize._reason_history: CHANGELOG.md and CHANGELOG_ru.md are append-only records of what shipped. They grow by one entry per release for as long as the project lives, and splitting them by size would put a version boundary wherever the five-hundredth line happened to fall. The cap exists so that a module stays comprehensible; a history is read by searching it, not by reading it through. The two are listed separately rather than exempting *.md, so a design document that grows past the cap still has to answer for it.
